headline: Evolutionary models and benchmarks extend to epistasis, orthology, lineage dating and protein language models
label: Computational Tools Molecular Evolution
summary: New tools pair ground-truth simulation and richer evolutionary models with accessible analysis platforms for protein and lineage evolution.
synthesis: The dominant thread is methodological infrastructure for molecular evolution: models that capture more biological structure and resources for testing or applying them. OrthoSimulator generates empirically calibrated datasets with known orthogroups and gene trees for benchmarking orthology inference. A continuous-time Gillespie model parameterized by a Potts generative model reports epistatic signatures, with epistasis slowing evolution. TyCHE links clock rates to discrete states for time-resolved B cell lineage trees and ships with the SimBLE simulator. A review covers protein foundation models for residue dependencies, pathogenicity and alignment-free analyses, while MolEvolvR packages domain-centric searches, phylogenies and domain architecture in a web app. What is new is the pairing of richer models with explicit simulators; the items differ in task and method, so this is not shared by all.
